notes: Mean pass rate: v2.1 0.987, v2.0 0.888, no skill 0.801 (n=15 each; 45 runs). Every expectation was decided by a fixed rule, without per-run judgment.

With the assertions added after iteration 1 removed (scope and residue in evals 1, 4 and 5), the scores are v2.1 0.983, v2.0 0.950 and no skill 0.883. Part of v2.1's lead comes from assertions written for its new rules.
Residue: __pycache__ was left in v2.1 0/12, v2.0 6/12 and no-skill 9/12 project runs. Unrequested docs/formats.md edits in eval 1: v2.1 0/3, v2.0 3/3, no skill 3/3.

Eval 5 (Python 3.11 target) did not trigger the trap. No run used itertools.batched, and every run, including no skill, ran python3.11, because the README names it explicitly. A subtler fixture is needed.
Eval 4: one v2.1 run skipped re-reading the file after the edit. Two of three no-skill runs never ran run_tests.py.
Cost: v2.1 63.7k tokens/run, v2.0 63.4k and no skill 53.1k. v2.1 is cheaper than v2.0 on edits (eval 4: -4k, eval 5: -2k) and more expensive on research (eval 3: +8k, from deeper source checks).

Grading bug found and fixed during this run: the exporter acceptance script created __pycache__ in candidate projects, which made residue look worse. Caches newer than each run's answer file were removed, the acceptance scripts now use -B and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, and grading was re-run twice with identical results.
